transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Lena Martinez (Redwood AE), Rahul Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Boreal CISO), Tom Alvarez (VP Eng), Sofia Ruiz (DevOps)

Summary: quick security posture discovery focused on SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments; customer wants clarification on data residency and retention, keys and HSM support, and an ask to run a short benchmark if Dedicated or Private chosen.

Topics: security attestations, network topology for Private, SSO and provisioning, key management, audit and logging retention, retention/deletion policies, regulatory constraints for patient PII, timeline for pilot.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, and Rahul will join on the security and deployment details. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good thanks, Maya here. Appreciate you taking the time, we wanted to go over security posture because we're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a patient-facing feature.
[00:15] Tom: Yep, Tom on my end. High level: low latency is important but we can't compromise on PHI controls or auditability.
[00:23] Rahul: Totally, quick intro from our side: we do hosted API which is fastest, Dedicated reserved pools for isolated capacity, and Private which can be VPC or on-prem. We'll focus on the controls you care about.
[00:35] Maya: Great. First question, do you have SOC 2 and ISO? We require both for our vendor shortlist.
[00:41] Lena: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. I can send the attestation packs after this call.
[00:47] Maya: Perfect. Can you also share scope? Does it include the serving runtime and key management?
[00:53] Rahul: The SOC2 covers the hosted control plane and the inference runtime for hosted customers. For Dedicated and Private, certain components fall under customer-managed scope — the report note will say that. We'll share the explicit scoping matrix.
[01:06] Tom: When you say Private, do you support customer-managed KMS / HSM? For our compliance we need customer keys.
[01:12] Rahul: Yes. Private supports customer KMS integration — AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault, and also HSM options via BYOK. For Dedicated we also offer a KMS integration path. For Hosted there's provider-managed keys but we do envelope encryption and customer can use a bring-your-own-key in some enterprise plans.
[01:31] Sofia: Is there any plaintext logging that could include model prompts or outputs? We need strict PII controls.
[01:36] Rahul: By default we redact PII in logs and we don't retain prompts beyond the configured retention. For Dedicated/Private your logs stay in your VPC or on your account. For the hosted plan we can opt out of data retention; there's a 'no retention' policy for enterprise customers.
[01:53] Maya: How granular is RBAC? We have multiple teams and need role separation between dev, ops, and audit.
[01:58] Lena: We support RBAC with roles and policies, SSO via SAML/SCIM provisioning, and per-route ACLs. Rahul, do you want to add the technical bits?
[02:06] Rahul: Sure — we integrate with SAML 2.0 SSO providers, SCIM for provisioning users/groups. RBAC can be enforced at org, project, and route levels. You can require MFA for certain roles, and audit logs show user and token-level events.
[02:19] Tom: Are audit logs tamper-proof? We need append-only and long retention for audits.
[02:23] Rahul: For Hosted we offer immutable logs with export to your SIEM (via syslog or S3 export). For Dedicated and Private, you control log storage so you can point to an immutable store. We can also ship signed audit exports if you need non-repudiation.
[02:36] Maya: What about network architecture for Private? Our security team will want a network diagram and to know if the control plane needs inbound access to our VPC.
[02:44] Rahul: Private has two modes: air-gapped on-prem package and VPC-hosted where control plane can be customer managed. For VPC option, we use private peering or customer-managed egress, minimal inbound, and all admin API calls are over a private link. We'll send a reference diagram.
[02:59] Sofia: Any specifics on firewall rules or ports? We have strict egress rules.
[03:03] Rahul: We'll provide a hardened list — typically HTTPS outbound and the usual management ports over private peering. No wide open inbound is required.
[03:11] Tom: For performance benchmarking, if we go Dedicated we want to test quantized model variants and see latency at our request pattern. How does Redwood handle model variants and fallbacks?
[03:20] Lena: Redwood can pin model versions and we have automatic fallback to compatible variants if capacity is constrained. Rahul can run a benchmark with your prompts on a dedicated pool and produce latency/cost metrics.
[03:31] Rahul: Yes, we can run a short perf run. We'll want a sample prompt set and target p50/p95 SLOs. Also note quantization profiles may change throughput; we'll recommend profiles.
[03:42] Maya: Okay good. On encryption at rest: algorithm details and key rotation policy?
[03:46] Rahul: We use AES-256 for data-at-rest with envelope encryption. Key rotation supported via KMS; rotation is customer controlled for BYOK. We'll document rotation frequency and our recommendations.
[03:57] Maya: For hosted, where are keys stored? If hosted is not acceptable we may need Private.
[04:02] Lena: Hosted uses provider-managed keys by default but enterprise customers can request BYOK with dedicated tenancy. If BYOK still isn't acceptable, Private on-prem is the path.
[04:12] Tom: Data residency — we need EU residency for some datasets. Does Redwood host in EU regions?
[04:17] Rahul: Yes, we have regional deployment options; hosted EU regions are available and Private can be deployed in your on-prem or cloud region. We'll include the region map.
[04:27] Sofia: Retention policy enforcement — can we automate deletion and proof of deletion for PII?
[04:33] Rahul: We support configurable retention windows per project and per dataset; for deletion we can produce deletion logs and a deletion certificate as part of audit exports.
[04:42] Maya: About SSO — we use Okta. Any known issues with SCIM provisioning?
[04:47] Lena: Okta is a supported provider. We've seen customers do SCIM provisioning for groups and map to RBAC roles without issues.
[04:54] Tom: On contract terms — do you offer data processing agreements and subprocessors list?
[04:58] Lena: Yes DPA included, and subprocessors list is part of our security attestation pack. We'll attach those docs.
[05:05] Maya: A few deeper questions from our security team: are model weights or cached KV accessible to Redwood employees? We're worried about any human access to customer prompts.
[05:15] Rahul: By default we run with strict access controls; engineer access requires approvals and is audited. Cached KV and runtime data are encrypted and access is logged. For Private deployments, no Redwood access unless explicitly granted.
[05:28] Maya: Could you describe your breach/incident response process? We need SLAs for incident notification.
[05:34] Lena: We have an incident response runbook; critical incidents have a 1-hour notification SLA and a designated security contact. We'll share the IR plan.
[05:42] Sofia: Does Redwood support token-level cost breakdowns and per-token attribution? We want to tie usage to teams and audit for costs.
[05:49] Rahul: Yes, token-level attribution in the console, and you can export usage per route/model for billing and audit.
[05:55] Tom: Any concerns about compliance certifications beyond SOC2/ISO for healthcare?
[05:59] Lena: We also have HIPAA controls and can support a BAA for customers with PHI requirements; we'll share our compliance statement.
[06:07] Maya: That's good. For the pilot what would you recommend as next steps?
[06:11] Lena: A typical path: we share SOC/ISO and DPA, you confirm scope, then a technical deep dive to run benchmarks on Dedicated or Private. If time permits, a short POC with audits enabled so you can verify logs and retention.
[06:23] Maya: Sounds sensible. We prefer Dedicated initially to keep managed service but isolated; if Dedicated meets our certs we'll look later at Private.
[06:31] Rahul: We'll prepare a Dedicated pilot runbook: instance types, target throughput, SLOs, and required test data.
[06:38] Tom: Can we get a reference architecture for Dedicated networking? We need to know the minimal attack surface.
[06:44] Rahul: Yes, that'll be in the guide. We'll include allowed IP ranges, private peering, and NAT egress patterns.
[06:52] Sofia: Any tips for tokenization and PII masking before sending prompts? We have a pre-processing pipeline.
[06:58] Rahul: We recommend client-side PII redaction where feasible and use structured prompt patterns to limit free text. We can provide sample pre-processing regex and a small library.
[07:08] Maya: For evidence we need to show auditors how log retention is enforced — is that automated?
[07:13] Rahul: Yes, retention enforcement is policy-driven and we can provide audited exports on schedule to your SIEM.
[07:20] Tom: A quick nit: does Redwood keep model evals or debug traces that include prompts?
[07:25] Lena: Debug traces are disabled by default for customer workloads; when enabled they're timeboxed and need explicit approvals.
[07:32] Maya: Ok, one more operational: who will own the pilot from Redwood side?
[07:37] Lena: I'll own the commercial side and Rahul will be the SE lead for the pilot.
[07:41] Maya: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:44] Tom: No, that's it from us.
[07:46] Lena: Great, recap of action items then: I'll send SOC2/ISO attestation, DPA and subprocessors; Rahul will send the Dedicated pilot runbook, KMS/HSM partner list, and network diagram; Sofia will share infra diagram and data retention policy. We'll schedule the technical deep dive next Tue April 13th.
[08:02] Maya: Sounds good, thanks.
[08:04] Rahul: Thanks all.

End of call.
